# Time and Space Science

> Free, no-sign-up clock tools and countdowns that run entirely in the browser.
> Static pages on Cloudflare Pages; no accounts, no tracking beyond analytics,
> nothing to install. 4209 pages in all.

Everything below is a real, permanent URL. Figures on time-and-sky pages are
computed, not scraped: the methodology pages state the method and its limits.

## Sections

- [Alarm clock](https://timeandspace.science/alarm-clock/) — 51 pages: Set an alarm for any time, in the browser. Includes a page per half-hour ('set an alarm for 6:30 AM').
- [Countdown timer](https://timeandspace.science/timer/) — 70 pages: A timer with a page per common duration and per use case (eggs, study, meditation).
- [Stopwatch](https://timeandspace.science/stopwatch/) — 2 pages: Stopwatch with laps, CSV/image export, and a four-way version for classrooms.
- [World clock](https://timeandspace.science/world-clock/) — 110 pages: Current time, UTC offset and DST state for a city, one page per city.
- [Time difference calculator](https://timeandspace.science/time-difference-calculator/): Hours and minutes between two clock times, in any time zone, daylight-saving aware.
- [12/24-hour clock converter](https://timeandspace.science/24-hour-clock-converter/) — 49 pages: Convert between the 12-hour clock and the 24-hour clock (military time), with a page per half hour.
- [Sunrise & sunset](https://timeandspace.science/sun/) — 1157 pages: Sunrise, sunset, day length and twilight for a city and any date. Includes an any-location page.
- [Moon](https://timeandspace.science/moon/) — 1237 pages: Moonrise, moonset, phase and illumination per city, plus phase calendars, eclipses, supermoons and blue moons.
- [Tide predictions](https://timeandspace.science/tides/) — 166 pages: Predicted tide times and heights for US NOAA stations, grouped by state and county.
- [Sun, Earth & Moon simulator](https://timeandspace.science/sun-moon-earth-movement-simulator/) — 1104 pages: Where the sun and moon are from a given place at a given instant, scrubbable over a day, week or month.
- [The planets](https://timeandspace.science/planets/): Every planet in orbital order with a picture and a couple of paragraphs each, the asteroid belt in its place, and a page for every one.
- [Solar system simulator](https://timeandspace.science/solar-system-simulator/) — 5 pages: The planets on their real orbits, with moon systems, the asteroid belt and comets.
- [Rocket launch simulator](https://timeandspace.science/rocket-launch-simulator/) — 4 pages: When the next launch window to Mars, Jupiter and Saturn opens, what it costs, and how the real missions compare.
- [Questions & concepts](https://timeandspace.science/concepts/) — 54 pages: One question per URL, answered in the first paragraph: why we have seasons, what causes tides, why the moon changes shape, what a time zone is — each with a computed drawing.
- [Glossary](https://timeandspace.science/glossary/): Every term on the site, A to Z, each linking to the question page that explains it.
- [Countdowns](https://timeandspace.science/countdown/): Countdown pages for holidays, celebrity birthdays, sports and anniversaries.
- [Events calendar](https://timeandspace.science/calendar/): Every countdown by month. Also published as a subscribable feed at /calendar/events.ics.
- [Methodology](https://timeandspace.science/methodology/) — 6 pages: How each figure on the site is worked out, and where it stops being reliable.
- [Classroom](https://timeandspace.science/classroom/) — 4 pages: The invitation to teachers: bring a lesson you're proud of, we develop it together — on our tools or tools we build for it — and publish it free for every teacher.

## Notes

- Tide predictions are NOAA CO-OPS astronomical predictions. They exclude
  weather, storm surge and atmospheric pressure, and are not for navigation.
- Sun and moon figures are computed in the browser, so they are never stale.
  Accuracy bounds are published at https://timeandspace.science/methodology/.
- The planetary positions are approximate Keplerian elements valid 1800-2050.
  They are not an ephemeris.
- Timers and alarms only ring while the page is open.
